candidates.searchIntent: Home-studio producers and DIY metal bands want to eliminate the boomy, blurry buildup between kick, bass, and low-tuned guitars while preserving aggressive sub-bass weight and punch.
candidates.angle: Generic mix advice tells producers to 'just high-pass at 100 Hz and duck the bass,' which cripples heavy guitar tones and destroys kick impact. We provide an aggressive metal-specific protocol: polarity checks first, frequency slotting (deciding who owns 50–70 Hz), split-frequency bass processing, and dynamic multiband compression on palm-mute buildup (200–350 Hz).
candidates.whyNow: Downtuned 7/8-string guitars and high-tempo double bass are standard in modern rock/metal, making low-end masking the single most frequent problem DIY producers seek help with across production forums and YouTube tutorials.
